<thought>The mass spectrum shows a prominent ion at m/z ≈ 121, which is consistent with the protonated molecular ion [M+H]⁺ of a compound with neutral mass ≈ 120 Da. The ¹H NMR displays five aromatic protons split into a 2 H multiplet at δ 7.47 and a 3 H multiplet at δ 7.64, the typical pattern for a monosubstituted benzene ring. A common monosubstituted aromatic compound with formula C₈H₈O (neutral mass ≈ 120 Da) is acetophenone (phenyl‑methyl‑ketone). Its protonated ion appears at m/z ≈ 121, matching the observed mass spectrum, and its aromatic protons give exactly the observed 2 H/3 H pattern. Therefore the most likely structure is acetophenone. Its SMILES representation is `CC(=O)C1=CC=CC=C1`. </thought>
<final_answer>CC(=O)C1=CC=CC=C1</final_answer>
